clue.text: Homeless Bedlamite in C17th song about toad in mid-summer

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked letters sit inside the middle of the other word

parts.note: the middle two letters of summer

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of toad are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A seventeenth-century ballad about a vagrant madman who sings of a toad at midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom o' Bedlam is the homeless madman of a seventeenth-century English ballad; Bedlam was London's asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad's wandering lunatic calls himself Mad Tom, a beggar released from the Bethlem hospital.

clue.text: Aesop's foible?

definitions.meaning: the ancient Greek storyteller whose every tale ends with a lesson

explanation.surface: A question about the weakness of the famous teller of animal tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Foible nearly echoes fable: Aesop's quirk was tacking a moral onto every story.
explanation.definitionFit: Moralism is the habit of preaching lessons about right conduct, which every Aesop fable ends with.

clue.text: Spike expressing surprise at El Chapo

explanation.definitionFit: El Chapo, Joaquín Guzmán, ran the Sinaloa cartel, a notorious narcotics boss.

clue.text: Love lion print

clue.text: It will do you good putting bits of muddy earth in the small truck

clue.text: New Indian guard, non-U, greeting PM

the letter itself
